originality.rationale: The elementary power-sum type-count formula is prior mathematics, including for the infinite-class analogue. The novelty assessed is only the complete fixed-base-size inverse classification for two through five represented classes; the previously available general moment counting does not state or immediately supply its sharp five-class fibers. The published homogeneous-multipartite classifications identify the ambient structures; the previously examined pure-equivalence type, random-bipartite switching, and metric-distance-profile results concern different invariants. Searches targeted equal sums of five powers of two, equal exponent sums, and multipartite one-point reconstruction. No equivalent all-size exact fiber theorem was located. value.rationale: A natural inverse question for the count of complete finite-parameter logical types admits a sharp classification: rigidity through four represented classes, exactly enumerated collision fibers for five classes at all sizes, and a minimal explicit sixteen-parameter obstruction. This is not a routine re-expression of the already known power-sum formula: identifying all equal-power-sum equal-exponent-sum multisets requires a finite but structural carry tree classification, valid for arbitrary size. A natural adjacency-graded refinement is fully reconstructive. The known base cardinality is an essential, explicit hypothesis.
